descriptors.R: nominee of the party that held the presidency from 1861 to 1885 and holds a majority in the Senate
descriptors.D: nominee of the party of the administration in office since 1885

compile_desc.R: the party that held the presidency from 1861 to 1885 and holds a majority in the Senate
compile_desc.D: the party of the administration in office since 1885

others_line: Other candidates on some ballots, including a Prohibition and a Union Labor nominee (answer "other").
never_name: Harrison, Cleveland, Morton, Thurman, Fisk, Streeter, Blaine or Sherman

slice_sources.men: 1880 and 1890 censuses interpolated to November 1888; men 21+ outside the eleven Southern states (including declarant aliens where they could vote); turnout and choice from the backbone, calibrated to certified 1888 returns.
slice_sources.women: 1880 and 1890 censuses interpolated to November 1888; women 21+ outside the South; no state let women vote for president in 1888 (women voted in Wyoming Territory, which had no electoral votes), so this slice casts no presidential vote.
slice_sources.south-white: 1880 and 1890 censuses interpolated to November 1888; white adults in the eleven former Confederate states (includes a small number of American Indian and Asian adults); calibrated to certified 1888 returns.
slice_sources.black-south: 1880 and 1890 censuses interpolated to November 1888; Black adults in the eleven former Confederate states; Black men still voted in large numbers, but violence, fraud, complex ballot laws and new poll taxes (Florida, 1889) cut their turnout; the shortfall against white turnout is counted as exclusion.
slice_sources.immigrants: 1880 and 1890 censuses interpolated to November 1888; foreign-born white adults who were aliens or had only declared their intent (first papers); declarant aliens could vote in several Midwestern and Western states (fewer each decade as states repealed it), so part of this slice could vote.

masks: the Senate majority party's campaign chairman
